topics.title: Understanding autism: myths, stereotypes and the spectrum
topics.scope: What autism is and is not: deficit vs difference models, empathy and masking myths, DSM-5 support levels, why 'high-functioning' is a bad label, the spectrum as a wheel of traits, history (Sukhareva, Wing) and media stereotypes.

topics.title: The double empathy problem: mutual misunderstanding between autistic and neurotypical people
topics.scope: Milton's double empathy theory vs mind-blindness, studies of autistic-neurotypical communication and first impressions, and how both sides can bridge the gap with openness and self-compassion.

topics.title: Autism and employment: strengths, barriers and workplace inclusion
topics.scope: Myths about autistic careers and teamwork, work strengths (detail focus, monotropism), Buckland Review statistics, barriers and recommendations, accommodations that help, and research on remote work and neuroinclusive teams.

topics.title: Sensory regulation, emotions and recovery for neurodivergent people
topics.scope: Stimming and its functions, the eight sensory channels including interoception, how autistic adults recognize and regulate emotions, and concrete sensory-based ways to relax and restore energy.

topics.title: Brain connectivity and subtypes in autism
topics.scope: Neuroscience of autism: connectivity theory of cell assemblies, synaptic pruning, hypo- vs hyperconnectivity, salience network findings in infants, fMRI-based autism subtypes, and the IL-17 fever effect.

topics.title: How the brain changes across the lifespan
topics.scope: Cambridge study of four brain turning points (9, 32, 66, 83), asynchronous cognitive peaks, adolescent synaptic pruning and shared risk for mental disorders, musicians' aging brains and human brain evolution.

topics.title: Emotion circuits: fear extinction, anger and aggression
topics.scope: How the amygdala learns and unlearns fear (competing neuron populations, dopamine-driven extinction as reward learning) and what brain research says about anger and aggression.

topics.title: Brain maintenance: waste clearance, mental fatigue and Alzheimer's links
topics.scope: Deep sleep and 40 Hz gamma stimulation driving glymphatic brain clearance, why hours of hard cognitive work build up glutamate and push toward short-term choices, and a fungal pathway to Alzheimer's-like pathology.

topics.title: The self, consciousness and free will
topics.scope: The 'I' as a brain model and useful illusion, critiques of IIT wording, Sapolsky's case against free will, measuring consciousness under anesthesia, and how alpha rhythms create the sense of body ownership.

topics.title: How perception works: from sensory fragments to meaning
topics.scope: How the brain assembles sensations into percepts (the dress, duck-rabbit), individual differences in color perception, the visually evoked auditory response, simultaneous vs successive perception and the left/right brain myth.

topics.title: Music and the brain
topics.scope: Why music moves us: biology of intonation, major/minor and rhythm, neural resonance and entrainment theory, universal note prediction, musicians' brains and sonification of stars.

topics.title: Group polarization, conformity and social norms
topics.scope: Why groups radicalize and people defend positions ever more fiercely, preference falsification, Asch/Milgram/Zimbardo reread, why rumors and memes spread, traditions and unwritten norms (Serbian hospitality) as system rigidity or balance, and masculinity as a shifting social norm (the 'crisis of masculinity' and men's double bind).

topics.title: Cooperation, game theory and the origins of morality
topics.scope: Prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, Axelrod's tournament and tit-for-tat, pseudo-dilemmas built on emotional pressure, plus how empathy, kindness and moral progress arise (de Waal, Pinker).

topics.title: Living under authoritarian regimes: compliance, denunciation and resistance
topics.scope: Why regimes get denunciations, why conscripts comply, asking who benefits instead of thinking in abstractions, double binds, witchcraft belief where institutions fail, and ridicule and whispered jokes as resistance.

topics.title: Small actions and social change: beating helplessness
topics.scope: Why the nirvana fallacy blocks action, historical cases where single actions led to big change, ripple effects and micro-legacies, and helping others as an antidote to helplessness and depression.

topics.title: Self-blame, overcontrol and the inner critic
topics.scope: How hindsight bias and error-correction produce self-blame, why 'I did my best' is a flawed frame, the costs of overcontrol (RO DBT), the 'good daughter' false self, satisficing over overcomplication, habit replacement and creators' restlessness.

topics.title: Evidence-based therapy approaches and choosing help
topics.scope: ACT and its hexaflex, Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy, harmful psychotherapies to avoid, choosing a self-help book for anxiety, a grounding practice for anxiety and insomnia, and free mental-health programs and lectures.

topics.title: Relationships, communication and repairing connection
topics.scope: Saying no with NVC, why familiar partners feel right, connection as exchange of shared facets and how to review a strained bond, the love-languages myth, Grice's conversational maxims, and how to support a hurt person (validation, attachment, restorative justice).

topics.title: Happiness, meaning and the good life
topics.scope: Why wishes fail to bring happiness (affective forecasting, adaptation, comparison), the hedonic treadmill, the experience machine, a psychologically rich life as a third axis, meaning as support against stress (Frankl), personal values, and checking happiness claims against sources.

topics.title: Hobbies, play and switching off
topics.scope: Why keep hobbies in a crisis, whether a hobby must counterbalance work (focused vs diffused mode), daily creative expression, reading without guilt, and lessons from a writing marathon.

topics.title: Large language models: capabilities, limits and risks
topics.scope: First impressions of ChatGPT, why it fails at arithmetic, hallucinations when summarizing papers, political biases in language models, citing AI, summarizers and video generators, and why states ban AI as a therapist.

topics.title: Human-machine interfaces and AI in science
topics.scope: Wearables that read faces and silent speech, an AI that moves the user's body, robotaxis, AI-designed proteins and antibiotics, Piaget-inspired robotics, and fiction about the human-machine future.

topics.title: Scientific thinking, philosophy and reading lists
topics.scope: What makes a science good (updatable, integrated, open), whether philosophy is useful, failed replication (LK-99), formative book lists and books on humanity's future, and free resources for reading research.

topics.title: Biomedical research news: aging, epigenetics and medicine
topics.scope: Short research digests: parabiosis and cryopreservation, epigenetic inheritance, aspartame and memory in mice, mitochondrial transplants, sex differences in strength training, TB and COVID public health lessons, digital twins of nervous systems, and entropy.

topics.title: Careers in psychology and science: from clinic to research
topics.scope: Working as a psychologist on online platforms abroad, moving from clinical practice into neuroscience, PhD survival skills from 'A PhD Is Not Enough', and first coding steps (MATLAB, Python) for research.
